defect.evidence_quote: Good law; the Miranda custody inquiry is objective (would a reasonable person feel free to terminate the interrogation and leave) and is a mixed question of law and fact. The §2254(d) habeas-review framework was later changed by AEDPA (1996); see Yarborough v. Alvarado for custody under AEDPA deference.
defect.locator_note: lake/Thompson v. Keohane__cbbfd6.json treatment.scope_note and treatment.varies_by_point
defect.problem: The good-law call is supported for the Miranda custody rule, but the assertion says varies_by_point=false while its own scope note says the §2254(d) habeas-review framework was later changed by AEDPA. That is a point-specific currency limitation.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep field_i_validity good_law for the objective Miranda custody/mixed-question rule, but set varies_by_point true and add a point override or explicit current-law caveat that Thompson's pre-AEDPA independent-review habeas point is superseded or limited for AEDPA cases.

reasons: Lake treatment field states good_law as of 2026-06-30 and no point_overrides.
The same disclosed scope note concedes AEDPA changed the §2254(d) framework, so a flat no-variation treatment label overstates currency for the habeas-review point.
Progeny edges include only proposed negative treatments with field_iii mentioned, so they do not by themselves prove Thompson is overruled.
residual_risks: The derivation metadata records R15 treatment audit required and cap_hit; a full external audit could refine treatment, but that evidence is outside the disclosed universe.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Split treatment into current substantive Miranda custody rule good law and pre-AEDPA habeas review standard superseded or limited by AEDPA.
